steps.text: When Magallan was little, there was a small flower shop on the corner near her home. She liked to visit.
Children would often buy flowers there, and ask the aging owner all sorts of questions.
Magallan enjoyed a song that the old man sang.

steps.name: Limping Old Man
steps.text: In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower♪

steps.name: Limping Old Man
steps.text: And my friend a-lies there, oh, and a-watches the snow come down♪

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: What does it mean? Is there really a place outside Columbia where hot water turns to ice as soon as you pour it out?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Have you been to any other special places?

steps.name: Limping Old Man
steps.text: Oh, you're interested, are you?

steps.name: Limping Old Man
steps.text: That would be another story altogether.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The icefields start here. I've walked this path many times, but it always feels different. I've never been so excited before!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Let's see how much the engine can take. Good, it hasn't frozen up yet, good work, Engineering. Maybe we can use it on the way up the mountain too?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And we better look over our supplies... alright. We're ready!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Magallan, you know that since the expedition decades ago, no one has tried to go any further beyond.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: This is a valuable opportunity. Go as far as you can and bring back as much data as possible!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Of course. This is my dream!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Going off the grid now. Magallan, over and out!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Are those footsteps?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is someone there?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whoa! Another ghost?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: W-Who's there?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Asbestos?!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hi, I'm...

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: This kid followed me because he was worried about me going by myself, and he damned near froze to death. I'm taking him back.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: I'm Bard, trainee operator in the Rhodes Island office. Operator Asbestos was picking up some medicine from me.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: According to regulations, I have to make sure that she leaves the office safely, but I got worried when she said she wanted to explore the icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, we're almost to the fields. And they're no place for the inexperienced. Don't put your life at risk.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: You know the way back. You can take it from here, I'm going with her.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: My name is Magallan, and I'm an operator from Rhine Lab stationed at Rhodes Island. Here's my badge.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm on a mission for Rhine, with plenty of supplies for two, including medicine for treating Infected symptoms. Operator Asbestos will be safe with me!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Oh, you're an operator from HQ? Alright then, you definitely have plenty of experience.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: But please return to the landship for a checkup after the trip, Operator Asbestos. I'll upload your data to the server.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Gah, fine.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Please be careful, Operator Magallan, and take care of Operator Asbestos.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I will. I'll take you part of the way. It's a pretty rough path.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So you went to the office for medication because you ran out in the field?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe, it's nice to have a familiar face on the trip.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But were you really coming to the icefields? Do you have enough supplies? If you only wanted to spook that guy, I'll send you right back.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ...Just send me back.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Ugh... forget it.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I was gonna go into the icefields, but I'm nowhere as prepared as you are.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I was in Columbia before this. I was headed back to the landship, but I didn't have enough medicine, so I got some by knocking out an office mission.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I heard an old man talking about the icefields on the way, and it piqued my interest.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: An old man talking about the icefields? Have you heard a song that goes, 'In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower♪'?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: From the old man?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You must've been close to my home! How's the old man doing? He sells really pretty flowers!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey, where are you going? We should be heading north.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Up the glacier.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A glacier has to be formed under the right conditions to be fit for climbing. You need heavy snowfall in the winter and a mild summer. Otherwise, you get dangerous cracks.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You call the shots in the Black Flow, but this is the icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I've been down this path hundreds of times as a Rhine field researcher. They send me out here because no one knows it better than me.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If you try to strike out on your own, I'll—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hey, don't cover your ears! I'm serious!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Asbestos! Hey, Asbestos!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I heard you!!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Look, I studied that ice pillar a few years ago.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: They're formed by intersecting cracks in the glaciers. They look solid from a distance, but you never know if they might suddenly collapse.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So we go around it. And we tie ourselves together with this safety cable. And you never, ever untie it under any circumstances.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Won't we drag the other one down if one of us slips?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If something happens to one of us, we can easily find the other and help out.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: There's no such thing as the individual on the icefields. An explorer joins her fate to the other, it's the only way to move forward.
Day by day, Magallan and Asbestos go deeper and deeper into the icefields.
Their interactions grow briefer as they save their strength to face the constant snowstorms.

a.text: 'Why do I challenge my limits? What will I find, what will I get, and what will remain?'

steps.text: Everyone knows it gets more dangerous the deeper you go. No one wants to lose her life until she sees what she truly wanted to see.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Tie the icepick tight! Hook onto the cracks in the rocks if you slip—don't untie the rope!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: You'll fall too!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I still have the drone. Shut up and listen for its signal, grab it, and relax your legs. One, two, three!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Rrrah!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Go up and find a place with good footing, then tie the rope on the screw so I can come up.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Done!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Good. Now, I—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: —Whoa!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Gotcha!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Coming up! The drone—

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: It fell.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Whew, at least we're alive. Why did you try to untie the rope?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We have rescue drones. Never untie the rope! Let me make a mark here in case someone else comes by...
A month passes.

Magallan has seen countless records. The dreams people have about the icefields come in many different forms: wealth, knowledge, power... but all she cares about is her childhood dream, the story of the song.
Beneath their feet, the icefield is no longer infinite and boundless, but a conquest made one step at a time.
Still, the end is nowhere in sight. It is hidden away in the snow, and anyone on the snow is at the mercy of the avalanches.
Footprints are gradually covered by the falling snow, but humans continue to tread on stubbornly.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Are you ok? How are the drones?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Down to the last one. Doesn't look like it'll last long though.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sensors detect a big rock ahead. Great place for a rest. With the data and samples we collected, we might want to set up an outpost here!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Looks like our explorer has a beautiful dream.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ...Is this the rock you were talking about?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yup! Even bigger than I thought. You don't see ice crystals this big very often. It's a miracle to have it preserved like that.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: There are carvings on it. Are those somebody's initials?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Carvings? How rude! Don't they know we leave only footprints?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But I don't know of any explorers who came here after the last icefield landing... hold on.
Magallan goes around the rock and observes the carvings from downwind.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I remember these initials from the records...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Could it be...?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: ...Asbestos, I think those who came before us are buried here.
Magallan starts digging at the snow and ice, first with her gloved hands, then with a shovel, then with her hands again.
Slowly, a frozen body emerges from beneath the snow, then another, and another. Asbestos joins in to help, and they excavate four bodies, laying them side-by-side on the snow.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I heard a team got in the icefields decades ago. I just didn't expect to find them here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We can't bring the bodies back, but I guess we can dig a proper grave. And we'll send their personal effects to their families.
The explorers' faces are young, frozen in time beneath the snow.
Their discoveries have inspired countless who came after them to continue to explore the icefields, including those who found their remains so they could see light of day one last time.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I think that's gonna be me, dying as an explorer.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sometimes I ask myself if I'm willing to lose my life on an expedition, if it means that science takes another step forward?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I've never found the answer, but I know that these pioneers before us were willing to go, no matter what.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I can't imagine the courage it would take. I would miss my parents and my friends; I don't want to lose my life, or lose my friends.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's a noble thing to sacrifice for one's ideals, but I don't want to see any friends die, as long as I can do anything about it.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: The wind's died down. I'll put up a tent.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'The skipper lost his toes to frostbite, then the entire right leg. Our sled broke down five days ago. Still he ploughs ahead. 'Twenty-three years!' he cries.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'We started with twenty-four. Now we're down to five, and it doesn't look like we're going to make it back.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'I can't feel my lower body anymore. That's how the skipper lost his leg. It just broke off with no blood at all. I can still move my hands, though.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'The skipper would have yelled at me, breathing white fog through his beard, the water vapor turning to ice on his beard strands. But he'll forgive me in the end.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'I'll write our names on this rock.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Peary, Abigail, Merlot, Abel, Colt. We write our names here on this great rock of the icefields, so that our deeds may live on forever.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'May nature forgive this final deed of the dying.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'It's time for me to sleep. Merlot closed her eyes a few minutes ago. It's a shame that we never made it to our wedding, but the snow makes for a fine dress.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Goodnight, my love.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Merlot was Columbian. Abigail was from Kjerag. The team came from many different countries...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It was always my dream to be part of a team like that.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: There's something else on the page...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'And my friend a-lies there, oh, and a-watches the snow come down.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So they knew the song too.

a.text: In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower♪
And my friend a-lies there, oh, and a-watches the snow come down♪

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Be at peace.

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Hiss—Hiss—

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Your communicator has been hissing non-stop. Can't you do something about it?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: My communicator? I haven't had a signal for days. Why would it make any noise at all?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wait, is it picking up something?

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Got the photo&%Maggy#@Thanks. Auroraa#&very beautif#¥stunning sorry can't*%better words@%%also saw#@

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I sent some photos to Aurora while I was exploring the icefields. Is she answering?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: How did we get that message here? We're so far from Rhodes Island!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's a miracle!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Aurora... the Ursus girl?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yup! She's amazing! The transmission is fragmented, but it's definitely a transmission alright!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Guys! I got a transmission here, that should be impossible! But it's from my friend, Aurora!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: She's a really cute white-haired Ursus girl from Kjerag. We made a promise to explore the icefields together when she gets better.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Hehe, thank you. It must be your doing that I got this message!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Asbestos! Aurora sent over some cheese fondue packs. It's a delicacy from her country. All we need to do is heat them up.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Wanna try? Aurora says it's perfect for cold weather. Let's eat up before the next snowstorm!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Cheese fondue? I won't stop you.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I think I have indigestion.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I could never get used to it.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's so rich... is this what they eat in Kjerag? In Columbia, we just put a little cheese on our hamburgers.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: I'm eating my own food.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I can't finish all of this...

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: It's not for Rim Billitonians. I'll see how far north we can go.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Day 29. Taught Asbestos the song. She sang it well. I'll teach Aurora next time!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Attempted to continue northward. Arrived at the waypoint today.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Finished going through the previous team's belongings. They contain information on many potential points of interest. I'll finish my forebears' unfinished work.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And realize my own dream.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Day 92. The new equipment is operating smoothly. Drone repairs are complete.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Attempted to progress north, but couldn't reach our waypoint due to inclement weather. We marked the furthest point we could reach; glacier crevasses beyond that point prevent us from progressing further.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We have surveyed most of the objectives identified by the previous team. We discovered several ruins and have finished collecting samples. We have marked the remaining locations that are out of reach.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The newest discovery is...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Day 132, our last day in the icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We did not reach the northmost waypoint, but with only one drone remaining and our gear severely damaged, we need to get replacements and prepare for the trip back.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I asked Asbestos and Aurora what they think when they see the icefields: conquering nature, or seeking one's own self, or joy at achieving a goal?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I came here to get closer to the story of the song I heard in my childhood.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's a choice that many have a hard time understanding. Asbestos mentioned getting into a big fight with her parents, and Aurora argued with her family too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm lucky to have parents who supported me, which allowed me to keep going despite my setbacks along the way.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The icefields are my dream. I want to make my dream come true, like those who came before me, who have no regrets about making the icefields their final resting place.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I have no regrets either.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: ...It's time to go.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So only the captain of the team made it back...

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Yes. His name was Peary, and the data he brought back were instrumental to further exploration. Many hail him as the first pioneer of the icefields.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: It means a lot that you brought back their things, even if the data may not be so important these days.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Rhine Lab will contact the authorities. We can leave the search for the next-of-kin to them. If there's no next-of-kin, their effects can be donated to museums, and we can get the media to hype things up as well.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Honoring them can only be a positive thing for the government and Rhine. Even though we didn't reach the northmost point, people will still know that Rhine has broken its own record again.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: The positive press will make better projects easier in the future. Great job, Magallan.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: All I wanted is to realize my dream, Polly...

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Of course; it's my dream too. But it's also a job, and you should take some time off after you take care of what you have on hand.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mom, how's the old man with a limp who runs the flower shop around the corner? The one that I used to go to when I was little.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That crepe shop I used to eat at hasn't changed at all.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Ah... the owner passed away a few months ago. His kids are thinking about selling the shop.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: I knew you were going to ask. He planted a lot of flowers on that field that you used to play on.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: They're in full bloom now, the entire field is covered.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: No need to hold things back if you're feeling sad. Want to have a look after dinner?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Here we are... the flowers look so nice.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is this the old man's headstone?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'And my friend a-lies there, oh, and a-watches the snow come down.'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Here ends my story. —Peary'

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: 'Peary'?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Mr. Peary... I met your team on the icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I went 800m past where I found them. Next time, I'm sure I can go even deeper.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: There was a friend with me. It was just the two of us, but I've made a lot of new friends. One of them, by the name of Aurora, is really interested in the icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It all started when... I became interested in the icefields after hearing your song. Now I've reached a place that you and your team never did.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Thank you. I...
Magallan wanted to leave something behind, but all she found was the notebook she carries with her.
There are no difficult formulas, no deep insights, only a true record of her feelings out on the icefields, and simple sketches of the sights she saw.
She takes it out and places it on the flower field. The grass and flowers embrace it, and the breeze flips its pages open.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: In an endless snowfield—ah! There's the bloom of a nameless flower♪

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And my friend a-lies there, oh, and a-watches the snow come down♪

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: It's getting late. I should go; it's a long way back to my house.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'll never stop exploring the icefields. I've sent your team's personal effects back to their families. Goodbye.

steps.name: Active Child
steps.text: Hey! Look what I told you! There's a really pretty flower field here that not many people know about!

steps.name: Running Child
steps.text: Wow! It's so beautiful!

steps.name: Active Child
steps.text: There are even more flowers up ahead! Have you ever climbed that rock? I was the first one to climb it!

steps.name: Running Child
steps.text: Race you there!

steps.name: Singing Child
steps.text: Hey, did someone drop a notebook?

steps.name: Singing Child
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Singing Child
steps.text: Wow... so that's what the northern icefields are like!

steps.name: Singing Child
steps.text: Sounds incredible...
